title: Arakhin 28
description: Why a man may dedicate some of his property but not all of it, the Usha rule on giving more than a fifth to charity, whether priests and Levites may dedicate, which priest receives a dedication, and a new mishna on dedications for priests, unspecified dedications and dedicating one’s own offerings.
topics: 💰 Twenty-one sela plus a fifth: when the owner redeeming a field takes precedence
📜 “Of all that he has”, but not all: why the verse names property, slaves, animals and fields
👧 Son, daughter, Hebrew slave, purchased field: one dedicates only what he may always sell
🤲 Usha: one who dispenses to charity should not dispense more than a fifth, and Rabbi Yeshevav and Rabbi Akiva
🏛️ Priests and Levites: Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi on land and movable property
🗓️ Which priest receives: any priest, the watch on duty, and a Jubilee that begins on Shabbat
🔔 The Jubilee and the Sabbatical Year release at once, the one at its beginning and the other at its end
🐂 Unspecified dedications, dedicating one’s own offerings, and a firstborn given to a daughter’s son

a1.he: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? דַּאֲמוּר בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְאֶחָד — הַבְּעָלִים קוֹדְמִין, וְאִם לָאו — אוֹמֵר לוֹ: הִגַּעְתִּיךָ.

a2.he: מַתְנִי׳ מַחֲרִים אָדָם מִצֹּאנוֹ וּמִבְּקָרוֹ, וּמֵעֲבָדָיו וּמִשִּׁפְחוֹתָיו הַכְּנַעֲנִים, וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּתוֹ, וְאִם הֶחְרִים אֶת כּוּלָּם אֵינָם מוּחְרָמִים, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מָה אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהַחְרִים כׇּל נְכָסָיו, עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם חָס עַל נְכָסָיו!

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ, ״מֵאָדָם״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אָדָם, ״מִבְּהֵמָה״ — וְלֹא כׇּל בְּהֵמָה, ״מִשְּׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה״ — וְלֹא כׇּל שְׂדֵה אֲחוּזָּה.

a4.he: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְרִים, וְאִם הֶחְרִים יְהוּ מוּחְרָמִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אַךְ״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: מָה אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי לְהַחְרִים כׇּל נְכָסָיו, עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה שֶׁיְּהֵא אָדָם חָס עַל נְכָסָיו!

a5.he: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מִכׇּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ״, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כֹּל דְּאִית לֵיהּ לָא לַחְרֵים, אֲבָל מִין אֶחָד לַיחְרְמֵיהּ כּוּלֵּיהּ, כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מֵאָדָם״ — וְלֹא כׇּל אָדָם.

a6.he: וְאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא ״מֵאָדָם״, דְּלָא סַגִּיא לֵיהּ בְּלָא עֲבוֹדָה, אֲבָל שָׂדֶה — סַגִּיא לֵיהּ בְּדִיסְתּוּרָן. וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָנֵי תַּרְתֵּי, מִשּׁוּם דְּהָכָא חִיּוּתָא וְהָכָא חִיּוּתָא, אֲבָל מְטַלְטְלִין — לַיחְרְמִינְהוּ כּוּלְּהוּ, צְרִיכִי.

a7.he: ״בְּהֵמָה״ לְמָה לִי? לְכִדְתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יַחְרִים אָדָם בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ, עַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִיִּים, וּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּהֵמָה״, מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ, אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ.

a8.he: וַהֲלֹא בִּתּוֹ קְטַנָּה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ, יָכוֹל יַחְרִימֶנָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״בְּהֵמָה״, מָה בְּהֵמָה יֵשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם, אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ רְשׁוּת לְמוֹכְרָהּ לְעוֹלָם.

a9.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: אִם לַגָּבוֹהַּ אֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי כּוּ׳. הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא!

a10.he: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דְּרַבִּי אִילָא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אִילָא: בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ, הַמְבַזְבֵּז אַל יְבַזְבֵּז יוֹתֵר מֵחוֹמֶשׁ.

a11.he: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לְבַזְבֵּז יוֹתֵר מֵחוֹמֶשׁ, וְלֹא הִנִּיחוּ לוֹ חֲבֵרָיו. וּמַנּוּ? רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב, וְלֹא הִנִּיחוּ לוֹ חֲבֵירָיו. וּמַנּוּ? רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.

a12.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּחְרִים בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ, וְעַבְדּוֹ וְשִׁפְחָתוֹ הָעִבְרִים, וּשְׂדֵה מִקְנָתוֹ — אֵין מוּחְרָמִין, שֶׁאֵין אָדָם מַחְרִים דָּבָר שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֶׁלּוֹ. הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהַלְוִיִּם אֵין מַחְרִימִין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּהֲנִים אֵין מַחְרִימִין — שֶׁהַחֲרָמִין שֶׁלָּהֶן, וְהַלְוִיִּם מַחְרִימִין — שֶׁאֵין הַחֲרָמִין שֶׁלָּהֶן.

a13.he: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּקַרְקָעוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הִיא לָהֶם״, וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּמִטַּלְטְלִין, שֶׁאֵין הַחֲרָמִין שֶׁלָּהֶן.

a14.he: גְּמָ׳ וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בִּשְׁלָמָא כֹּהֲנִים אֵין מַחְרִימִין — שֶׁחֲרָמִין שֶׁלָּהֶן, אֶלָּא לְוִיִּם, בִּשְׁלָמָא מְקַרְקְעֵי לָא מַחְרְמִי — דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי אֲחוּזַּת עוֹלָם הִיא לָהֶם״, אֶלָּא מִטַּלְטְלֵי לַיחְרְמֻי! אָמַר קְרָא: ״מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר לוֹ... וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״ — מַקִּישׁ מִטַּלְטְלִין לְקַרְקָעוֹת.

a15.he: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, בִּשְׁלָמָא כֹּהֲנִים — כְּדַאֲמַרַן, אֶלָּא לְוִיִּם, בִּשְׁלָמָא מְטַלְטְלִים לַחְרֵים — דְּלָא מַקֵּישׁ, אֶלָּא מְקַרְקְעֵי אַמַּאי? הָכְתִיב ״אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הִיא לָהֶם״! מַאי ״מַחְרִימִין״ נָמֵי דְּקָאָמַר? מִטַּלְטְלֵי.

a16.he: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בִּמְקַרְקְעֵי וְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּמִטַּלְטְלֵי, מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְקַרְקְעֵי נָמֵי קָאָמַר? הָכִי קָאָמַר: אָמַר רַבִּי: נִרְאִין דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בְּקַרְקָעוֹת, שֶׁאַף רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא נֶחְלַק אֶלָּא בְּמִטַּלְטְלִין, אֲבָל בְּקַרְקָעוֹת מוֹדֵה לֵיהּ.

a17.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין: הֶחְרִים מְטַלְטְלִין — נוֹתְנָן לְכׇל כֹּהֵן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל

b1.he: לְךָ יִהְיֶה״. הֶחְרִים שְׂדוֹתָיו — נוֹתְנָן לַכֹּהֵן שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ מִשְׁמָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״, וְגָמַר ״לַכֹּהֵן״ ״לַכֹּהֵן״ מִגֶּזֶל הַגֵּר.

b2.he: וְהָתָם מְנָלַן? דְּתַנְיָא: ״לַה׳ לַכֹּהֵן״ — קְנָאוֹ הַשֵּׁם וּנְתָנוֹ לַכֹּהֵן שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ מִשְׁמָר.

b3.he: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר לַכֹּהֵן שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ מִשְׁמָר, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְכׇל כֹּהֵן שֶׁיִּרְצֶה? כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר: ״מִלְּבַד אֵיל הַכִּיפֻּרִים אֲשֶׁר יְכַפֶּר בּוֹ עָלָיו״, הֲרֵי בְּכֹהֵן שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ מִשְׁמָר הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר.

b4.he: שָׂדֶה הַיּוֹצְאָה לַכֹּהֲנִים בַּיּוֹבֵל, נוֹתְנָהּ לַמִּשְׁמָר שֶׁפָּגַע בּוֹ יוֹבֵל. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: פָּגַע בּוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת, מַאי? אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחוּלְפָּנָא: נוֹתְנָהּ לַמִּשְׁמָר הַיּוֹצֵא.

b5.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תַּנְיָא, נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה אוֹמֵר, אֶחָד יוֹבֵל וְאֶחָד שְׁבִיעִית מְשַׁמְּטִין כְּאֶחָד, אֶלָּא שֶׁיּוֹבֵל בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ וְהַשְּׁמִטָּה בְּסוֹפָהּ.

b6.he: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִשּׁוּם הָכִי הֲוַאי! אֵימָא: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל כּוּ׳.

b7.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא שְׁבִיעִית בְּסוֹפָהּ, דִּכְתִיב: ״מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים תַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁמִטָּה״, אֶלָּא יוֹבֵל בִּתְחִילָּתוֹ? בְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים הוּא, דִּכְתִיב: ״בַּיּוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים תַּעֲבִירוּ שׁוֹפָר בְּכׇל אַרְצְכֶם״! הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא, דְּאָמַר: מֵרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הוּא דְּחָיֵיל יוֹבֵל.

b8.he: שַׁמְעַהּ חִזְקִיָּה בַּר בִּילְוָטִי, וַאֲזַל אֲמַר קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: וְלַיקֵּישׁ מִטַּלְטְלֵי לְקַרְקָעוֹת!

b9.he: לָאו תַּנָּאֵי הִיא? דְּאִיכָּא דְּמַקֵּישׁ, וְאִיכָּא דְּלָא מַקֵּישׁ, כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר: ״לָא מַקְּשִׁינַן״.

b10.he: מַתְנִי׳ חֶרְמֵי כֹּהֲנִים, אֵין לָהֶם פִּדְיוֹן, אֶלָּא נִותָּנִים לַכֹּהֲנִים כִּתְרוּמָה. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר: סְתַם חֲרָמִים לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״.

b11.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: סְתַם חֲרָמִים לַכֹּהֲנִים, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״. אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר ״כׇּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״? שֶׁחָל עַל קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְעַל קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים.

b12.he: מַחְרִים אָדָם אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו, בֵּין קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים בֵּין קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, אִם נֶדֶר — נוֹתֵן דְּמֵיהֶן.

b13.he: וְאִם נְדָבָה, נוֹתֵן אֶת טוֹבָתָן. ״שׁוֹר זֶה עוֹלָה״ — אוֹמְדִין כַּמָּה אָדָם רוֹצֶה לִיתֵּן בְּשׁוֹר זֶה לְהַעֲלוֹתוֹ עוֹלָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי.

b14.he: הַבְּכוֹר, בֵּין תָּם בֵּין בַּעַל מוּם — מַחְרִימִין אוֹתוֹ, וְכֵיצַד פּוֹדִים אוֹתוֹ? אוֹמְדִין כַּמָּה אָדָם רוֹצֶה לִיתֵּן בִּבְכוֹר זֶה לִיתְּנוֹ לְבֶן בִּתּוֹ אוֹ לְבֶן אֲחוֹתוֹ.

messages.text: Continued from 27b: the mishna’s case where the owner offers twenty sela for his consecrated field and another person offers twenty-six. Rav Sheshet explained the extra dinar: the owner wished from the outset to give an amount that reaches thirty-one sela and a dinar.

What are the circumstances of such an offer? It is in a case where the owner initially said he would purchase the field for twenty-one sela. In such an instance, the additional one-fifth amounts to five sela and one dinar, which means that the total payment of the owner is twenty-six sela and one dinar, greater than the offer of the other person. Accordingly, the owner takes precedence, and when the one-fifth is added to the twenty-six sela offer of the other person, the total price paid by the owner is equal to thirty-one sela and one dinar.

notes.he: דהוי בין קרן בין חומש כ"ו ודינר וזה מוסיף ה' היינו ל"א ודינר:
notes.en: What are the circumstances? Where they said twenty-one: so that principal and fifth together come to twenty-six and a dinar; and this one adds five [the fifth, to the other man’s twenty-six], which is thirty-one and a dinar.

notes.he: דאי הוה יהבינן ליה להאי הוה פסיד הקדש דינר ממאי דאמור ברישא הלכך הדרי אבעלים על כרחייהו:
notes.en: The owner takes precedence: for if we gave it to this other man, the Temple would lose a dinar compared with what [the owner] offered first. Therefore we go back to the owner, even against his will.

messages.text: And if the payment of the owner does not exceed the offer of the other person even when accounting for the additional one-fifth, then the treasurer says to the other person: The field has come into your possession.

notes.dh: ואם לאו אומר לו לזה הגעתיך
notes.he: דאמרי בעלים אתא גברא בחריקן:
notes.en: And if not, he says to this one: It has come to you: for the owner says: A man has come in my place [literally, into our breach].

notes.he: לזה תן אתה כ"ו שקלים והגיעתך]:
notes.en: And if not, he says to him: to this one: You give twenty-six shekels, and it has come to you.

messages.text: Mishna

A person may dedicate, for sacred or priestly use, some of his flock and some of his cattle, and some of his Canaanite slaves and maidservants, and some of his ancestral field. But if he dedicated all that he has of any type of property, they are not dedicated, i.e., the dedication does not take effect; this is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

notes.he: מקצת צאנו אומר הרי הן חרם ונותנן לכהן:
notes.en: Mishna. Of his flock: some of his flock. He says, “These are ḥerem,” and gives them to the priest.

notes.he: שלא שייר לעצמו כלום:
notes.en: All of them: so that he left nothing for himself.

notes.dh: מחרים אדם קצת מצאנו ומבקרו כו'
notes.he: לשם שמים שיכול לומר הרי הם חרם עלי ונתפסין:
notes.en: A person may dedicate some of his flock and his cattle etc.: for the sake of Heaven, in that he can say, “These are ḥerem for me,” and they take effect.

messages.text: If for the Most High a person may not dedicate all his property, it is all the more so the case that a person should spare his property and not give all of it to others.

notes.he: שלא יבזבזם להדיוט:
notes.en: That a person should spare his property: so as not to squander it on ordinary people.

notes.dh: על אחת כמה וכמה שיהא אדם חס על נכסיו
notes.he: כנגד הדיוט שלא יבזבז אותן להדיוט שלא יתנם כולם לאחרים שישייר לעצמו כלום מהיכן יחיה:
notes.en: All the more so that a person should spare his property: as regards ordinary people, that he should not squander it on ordinary people and not give all of it to others, but leave something for himself; [otherwise,] from what will he live?

messages.text: Gemara

From where are these matters, stated in the mishna, derived? This is as the Sages taught in a baraita, with regard to the verse: “Notwithstanding, no dedicated thing that a man may dedicate to the Lord of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:28).
messages.quote: But if he dedicated all that he has of any type of property, they are not dedicated

verse.he: אַךְ־כׇּל־חֵרֶם אֲשֶׁר יַחֲרִם אִישׁ לַיהֹוָה מִכׇּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ מֵאָדָם וּבְהֵמָה וּמִשְּׂדֵה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ לֹא יִמָּכֵר וְלֹא יִגָּאֵל כׇּל־חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ־קׇדָשִׁים הוּא לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But of all that anyone owns, be it human or animal or land-holding, nothing that has been proscribed for GOD may be sold or redeemed; every proscribed thing is totally consecrated to GOD.

messages.text: The verse indicates that one may dedicate “of all that he has” but not all that he has; likewise “of man” but not every man, i.e., not every slave of his; “of man or animal” but not every animal of his; and finally one may dedicate “of his ancestral field” but not all of his ancestral field.

notes.he: היינו מטלטלין ולא כל מטלטלין:
notes.en: Gemara. “Of all that he has”: this is movable property, and not all movable property.

notes.he: עבדים הכנענים:
notes.en: “Of man”: Canaanite slaves.

notes.dh: דתנו רבנן מכל אשר לו ולא כל אשר לו
notes.he: וא"ת והא האי קרא בחרם הניתן לכהנים כתיב דהא בסיפיה דקרא כתיב לא ימכר ולא יגאל ואילו חרמי בדק הבית יש להם פדיון כהקדש והיכי קאמר במתני' ומה אם לגבוה כו' והא לאו לגבוה הוא כי אם לכהנים ועוד דאיכא בפרק השולח (גיטין דף לח:) מאדם אלו עבדיו ושפחותיו הכנענים ופריך מינה לרב דאמר המקדיש עבדו יצא לחירות דלמיהוי עם קדוש קאמר ומאי קפריך והא בחרמים אין בהן קדושת הגוף ולא דמי למקדיש לומר דלמיהוי עם קדוש קאמר וי"ל דאפי' בחרמים הניתנין לכהנים יש בהן קדושת הגוף כדתני לקמן בפירקין (ערכין דף כט.) חרמים כל זמן שהן בבית בעלים הרי הן כהקדש לכל דבריהם נתנם לכהן הרי הן כחולין אלמא אית בהו קדושת הגוף:
notes.en: As the Sages taught: “Of all that he has,” and not all that he has: You might ask: this verse is written about a ḥerem given to the priests, since the end of the verse says “It shall not be sold or redeemed,” whereas dedications for Temple maintenance have redemption, like consecrated property. So how can the mishna say, “If for the Most High…”? This is not for the Most High but for the priests. Furthermore, in chapter HaSholeaḥ (Gittin 38b) it is taught: “Of man”: these are his Canaanite slaves and maidservants, and from this the Gemara challenges Rav, who said that one who consecrates his slave sets him free, because he meant that the slave should become one of the holy people. What is the challenge? Ḥeramim have no sanctity of the body, so they are not comparable to one who consecrates, of whom one can say he meant that the slave should become one of the holy people. One may answer that even ḥeramim given to the priests have sanctity of the body, as is taught later in this chapter (29a): Ḥeramim, so long as they are in the owner’s house, are like consecrated property in every respect; once he has given them to the priest, they are like non-sacred property in every respect. Evidently they have sanctity of the body.

messages.text: It might have been thought that one may not dedicate all his properties ab initio, but if he did dedicate all of them, they should be dedicated. Therefore the verse states: “Notwithstanding,” to teach that they are not dedicated. This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

notes.he: אכין ורקין מיעוטין:
notes.en: “Notwithstanding” [akh]: [the words] akh and rak are restrictions.

notes.he: [ת"ל אך וכל אכין ורקין מיעוטין:
notes.en: The verse states “notwithstanding” [akh]: akh and rak are restrictions.

messages.text: If for the Most High a person may not dedicate all his property, it is all the more so the case that a person should spare his property and not give it all to others.

And it is necessary to derive this halakha with regard to all the categories in the verse. As, if the Merciful One had written only: “Of all that he has,” I would say that one may not dedicate all that he has, but let him dedicate all of one type of property. Therefore, the Merciful One writes “of man,” to teach that he may not dedicate every man.

And if the Merciful One had written only: “of man,” one might say that he may not dedicate all of his slaves, as it is not possible for him to be without a slave to perform his work; but with regard to a field, it is possible for him to maintain a livelihood by sharecropping [distoran].

notes.he: שיהא אריס לאחרים ויקבל שדות למחצה ולשליש ולרביע:
notes.en: By sharecropping [distoran]: he becomes a tenant farmer for others, taking fields for a half, a third or a quarter [of the crop].

notes.he: (אמאי) [הוה אמינא] ליחרם כל שדותיו דסגיא ליה בדיסתורן שיכול ליקח שדות של אחרים באריסות ויכול לחיות בהן]:
notes.en: But a field: [I would have said] let him dedicate all his fields, for sharecropping is enough for him: he can take other people’s fields in tenancy and live from them.

notes.he: גרידא הוה אמינא משום הכי לא ליחרמינהו לכולהו שדותיו משום דחיותיה מינייהו אבל מאדם אימא ליחרמינהו לכולהו עבדין דסגיא ליה בשמעא בעלמא:
notes.en: And had it taught us field alone, I would have said that this is why he may not dedicate all his fields, because his livelihood comes from them; but as for “of man,” say he may dedicate all his slaves, since a mere attendant is enough for him.

messages.text: And if the Torah had taught this halakha with regard to only these two types, i.e., ancestral fields and slaves, one might say these may not be dedicated in their entirety because here there is livelihood and here there is also livelihood. But in the case of movable property, on which maintaining a livelihood does not depend, let him dedicate all of them. Therefore, all of these derivations are necessary.

notes.he: כתב רחמנא מכל אשר לו ולא כל אשר לו דהיינו מטלטלין:
notes.en: But movable property, say he may dedicate all of it: [so] the Merciful One wrote “of all that he has,” and not all that he has, which is movable property.

notes.he: משום דהכא והכא חיותיה דבין שדות ובין עבדים אין אדם יכול לחיות בלא שדה ובלא עבדים ואם יחרים כל עבדיו אינן מצויין עבדים [אחרים] טובים תדיר לקנות אבל מטלטלין דשכיחי מטלטלין אחרים למיזבן בכל שעה שירצה אימא ליחרמינהו כולהו כתב רחמנא מכל אשר לו ולא כל:
notes.en: Because here and here there is livelihood: in both fields and slaves, for a person cannot live without a field and without slaves; and if he dedicates all his slaves, other good slaves are not always available to buy. But movable property, since other movables are available to buy whenever he wishes, say he may dedicate all of it. [So] the Merciful One wrote “of all that he has,” and not all.

messages.text: Why do I need for the verse to state “or animal”? It is necessary for that which is taught in a baraita:

One might have thought a person can dedicate his son or his daughter, his Hebrew slave or maidservant, or his purchased field. Therefore, the verse states “animal” to teach that just as an animal is an item that he has permission to sell, so too, one can dedicate any item that he has permission to sell. He cannot dedicate an item that he does not have the ability to sell.

notes.he: למוכרה לחלוטין ורשאי להחרים למעוטי בנו ובתו עבדו ושפחתו העברים ושדה מקנה שאינו רשאי למוכרן:
notes.en: Just as an animal, which he has the right to sell outright, he may dedicate: to exclude his son and his daughter, his Hebrew slave and maidservant, and a purchased field, which he may not sell [outright].

messages.text: But in the case of his minor daughter, he has permission to sell her as a Hebrew maidservant. If so, one might have thought he may dedicate her. Therefore, the verse states “animal,” indicating that just as an animal is an item that he always has permission to sell, so too, one can dedicate any item that he always has permission to sell, whereas one may not sell his daughter once she reaches majority. A field as well can be sold only until the Jubilee Year.

notes.he: בתו יש לו רשות למוכרה בקטנותה ולא בנערותה:
notes.en: His daughter: he has the right to sell her while she is a minor, but not once she is a young woman [na’ara].

notes.dh: (אלא) [ת"ל] בהמה מה בהמה יש לו רשות למכור לעולם
notes.he: וא"ת א"כ שדה אחוזה נמי שהרי אם מכרה חוזרת לבעלים ביובל וי"ל דמ"מ יש לו רשות להוציא מידו לעולם כגון אם הקדישה וגאלה אחר שמתחלקת לכהנים ביובל א"נ י"ל דה"פ מה בהמה יש לו רשות למוכרה ושדה אחוזה נמי כל זמן שהיא בידו יכול הוא למוכרה משא"כ בבתו דמשתגדיל אין לו רשות למוכרה:
notes.en: The verse states “animal”: just as an animal he has the right to sell forever: You might ask: if so, an ancestral field too [should be excluded], since if he sells it, it returns to the owner at the Jubilee. One may answer that in any case he has the right to remove it from his possession forever, for example if he consecrated it and another person redeemed it, so that it is divided among the priests at the Jubilee. Alternatively, one may answer that this is the meaning: just as he has the right to sell an animal, so too an ancestral field, as long as it is in his possession, he can sell; which is not so of his daughter, whom he has no right to sell once she has grown up.

notes.dh: [או הואיל ורשאי למכור בתו קטנה יכול יחרימנה ת"ל בהמה] מה בהמה כו'
notes.he: למעוטי בתו שאינו רשאי למוכרה אלא (עד שהיא) בקטנותה אבל משבגרה שוב אינו רשאי למוכרה:
notes.en: [Or, since he may sell his minor daughter, might he dedicate her? The verse states “animal”:] Just as an animal etc.: to exclude his daughter, whom he may sell only while she is a minor; once she has grown up he may no longer sell her.

messages.text: This is identical to the opinion of the first tanna, i.e., Rabbi Eliezer, who prohibits the dedication of all one’s property.
messages.lead: § The mishna teaches that Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said: If for the Most High a person may not dedicate all his property, it is all the more so the case that one should spare his property and not give it all to others.
messages.quote: If for the Most High a person may not dedicate all his property

notes.he: ת"ק נמי אמר אם החרים את כולן אינן מוחרמין:
notes.en: This is the first tanna: the first tanna also said that if he dedicated all of them, they are not dedicated.

messages.text: There is a practical difference between them with regard to the statement of Rabbi Ila,
messages.quote: This is identical to the opinion of the first tanna

messages.text: In Usha the Sages instituted that one who dispenses his money to charity should not dispense more than a fifth.

notes.he: לעניים:
notes.en: One who dispenses: to the poor.

messages.text: Rabbi Eliezer, who did not state that one should spare his property, rules that one may give all his money to charity, provided he keeps a small portion for himself, whereas Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya maintains that one should not give more than a fifth.

notes.he: דגמרינן מיעקב דכתיב ביה תרין עישורין. ר' אלעזר בן עזריה אית ליה דרבי אילא דהא אתא לאשמועינן שיהא אדם חס על נכסיו ר"א לית ליה דרבי אילא דאי בזבז טובא לא איכפת לן אלא ששייר לעצמו קצת דומיא דחרם:
notes.en: A fifth: for we learn it from Jacob, of whom two tenths are written [“I will surely give a tenth,” Genesis 28:22, doubles the word]. Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya holds the view of Rabbi Ila, since he came to teach us that a person should spare his property. Rabbi Eliezer does not hold the view of Rabbi Ila: if one dispensed a great deal we are not concerned, so long as he left a little for himself, as with ḥerem.

notes.he: במסכת כתובות המבזבז את נכסיו לצדקה אל יבזבז יותר מחומש שלא יצטרך לבריות ת"ק דלא אמר יהא אדם חס לית ליה דר' אילא אלא אם ישייר לעצמו קצת יכול להחרים כל השאר ור' אלעזר בן עזריה דאמר יהא אדם חס אית ליה דר' אילא שיהא חס ואל יבזבז יותר מן החומש:
notes.en: There is a difference between them regarding Rabbi Ila, who said in tractate Ketubot: One who dispenses his property to charity should not dispense more than a fifth, so that he will not come to need other people. The first tanna, who did not say “a person should spare,” does not hold Rabbi Ila’s view; rather, if he leaves a little for himself he may dedicate all the rest. And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, who said “a person should spare,” holds Rabbi Ila’s view, that he should spare [his property] and not dispense more than a fifth.

messages.text: There was an incident involving a certain individual who sought to dispense more than a fifth of his property as charity, and his friend did not let him act upon his wishes. And who was this friend? It was Rabbi Yeshevav.

notes.he: שבקש לבזבז יותר מחומש]:
notes.en: Who sought to dispense more than a fifth.

messages.text: And some say it was Rabbi Yeshevav who wanted to give too much charity, and his friend did not let him do so. And who was the friend? It was Rabbi Akiva.
Mishna

In the case of one who dedicates his son or his daughter, or his Hebrew slave or maidservant, or his purchased field, those items are not considered dedicated, as a person may not dedicate an item that is not his.

notes.dh: שאין אדם מחרים דבר שאינו שלו
notes.he: דעבדו ושפחתו העברים ושדה מקנה חוזרין ביובל:
notes.en: For a person may not dedicate an item that is not his: since his Hebrew slave and maidservant and a purchased field go out at the Jubilee.

messages.text: Priests and Levites may not dedicate their property; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

notes.he: נכסיהן שאין נוהג בהן דין חרמים כדמפרש לקמן:
notes.en: Priests and Levites may not dedicate: their property, for the law of ḥeramim does not apply to it, as is explained below.

messages.text: Priests may not dedicate their property, as all dedicated property is theirs; it is one of the priestly gifts, as the verse states: “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours” (Numbers 18:14). But Levites may dedicate their property, as dedicated property is not theirs.

verse.en: Everything that has been proscribed in Israel shall be yours.

notes.he: דכתיב כל חרם בישראל וגו' וכיון דדידיה הוא מה הנאה בכך אי הוה מחרים איהו גופיה זכי ביה ולא יהב ליה לכהן אחר:
notes.en: Mishna. For the dedications are theirs: as it is written, “Everything dedicated in Israel [shall be yours].” And since it is his, what is gained by it? If he dedicated it, he himself would acquire it and would not give it to another priest.

notes.he: מה יתרון אם היה מחרים היה שלו שחרמים לכהנים:
notes.en: For the dedications are theirs: what advantage is there? If he dedicated it, it would be his, since dedications go to the priests.

messages.text: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears to be correct with regard to land, as it is stated about the land of the Levites: “But the fields of the open land surrounding their cities may not be sold, as that is their perpetual possession” (Leviticus 25:34), and they cannot renounce that land.

verse.he: וּשְׂדֵה מִגְרַשׁ עָרֵיהֶם לֹא יִמָּכֵר כִּי־אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם הוּא לָהֶם׃ {ס}
verse.en: But the unenclosed land about its cities cannot be sold, for that is its holding for all time.

notes.he: דלוים אין מחרימין בקרקעות:
notes.en: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears correct: that Levites may not dedicate land.

notes.he: דאמר לויים אין מחרימין בקרקעות דכתיב כי אחוזת עולם הוא להם:
notes.en: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears correct: who said that Levites may not dedicate land, as it is written, “For that is their perpetual possession.”

messages.text: And the statement of Rabbi Shimon appears to be correct with regard to movable property, which the Levites may dedicate, as dedicated property is not theirs. It is a gift for the priests, not the Levites.

notes.he: שהרי אין החרמים שלהן הלכך אי מחרימי מטלטלין חיילא עלייהו חרם ויהבי להו לכהנים:
notes.en: And the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to movable property: since the dedications are not theirs. Therefore, if they dedicate movable property, the ḥerem takes effect on it and they give it to the priests.

notes.he: ודברי ר' שמעון דאמר לוים מחרימין במטלטלין הואיל ואין חרמין שלהן אלא של כהנים הלכך מחרימין]:
notes.en: And the statement of Rabbi Shimon, who said that Levites may dedicate movable property: since the dedications are not theirs but the priests’, therefore they may dedicate.

messages.text: Gemara

And as for Rabbi Yehuda, what is his reasoning? Granted, priests may not dedicate property, as dedicated property is theirs; it is one of the gifts of the priesthood. But why are Levites unable to dedicate their property? Granted, they may not dedicate land, as it is written: “As that is their perpetual possession” (Leviticus 25:34). But let them dedicate movable property.
messages.quote: Priests and Levites may not dedicate

messages.text: The verse states: “Notwithstanding, no dedicated thing, that a man may dedicate to the Lord of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:28). The verse juxtaposes the dedication of movable property to that of land. Accordingly, as Levites cannot dedicate land, they cannot dedicate movable property either.

notes.he: מה קרקעות אין מחרימין אף מטלטלין נמי:
notes.en: And movable property is juxtaposed to land: just as land may not be dedicated, so too movable property.

messages.text: And with regard to Rabbi Shimon, what is his reasoning? Granted, priests may not dedicate their property, as we stated above, because dedicated property is theirs. But why may Levites dedicate their property? Granted, let them dedicate movable property, as Rabbi Shimon does not juxtapose movable property to land. But why may Levites dedicate land? Isn’t it written: That is their perpetual possession?
messages.quote: But Levites may dedicate their property

messages.text: What does Rabbi Shimon mean when he says Levites may dedicate property? He means they may dedicate only movable property.

But from the fact that the latter clause of the mishna teaches: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said the statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears to be correct with regard to land, and the statement of Rabbi Shimon appears to be correct with regard to movable property; by inference one may conclude that Rabbi Shimon also says Levites can dedicate their land.
messages.quote: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears to be correct with regard to land

notes.he: גמ' מדאיצטריך ליה לרבי למימר במטלטלין נראין דברי ר"ש דמשמע אבל בקרקעות אין נראין דבריו מכלל דאקרקעות נמי פליגי:
notes.en: Gemara. [From the latter clause:] since Rabbi needed to say “the statement of Rabbi Shimon appears correct with regard to movable property,” which implies that with regard to land his statement does not appear correct, by inference they disagree about land too.

notes.dh: [והא מדקתני סיפא אמר ר' נראין דברי ר' יהודה בקרקעות ודברי ר' שמעון במטלטלין
notes.he: ר' דהוה מכריע קאמר הכי נראין אבל מכלל דר' שמעון גופיה מקרקעי נמי קאמר דלויים מחרימין:
notes.en: But from that which the latter clause teaches, “Rabbi said: The statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears correct with regard to land and the statement of Rabbi Shimon with regard to movable property”: Rabbi, who was deciding between them, says “appears”; but by inference Rabbi Shimon himself also says of land that Levites may dedicate it.

messages.text: This is what the mishna is saying: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said that the statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears to be correct even to Rabbi Shimon with regard to land belonging to Levites, as even Rabbi Shimon disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda about the ability of Levites to dedicate property only with regard to movable property. But with regard to land, Rabbi Shimon concedes to Rabbi Yehuda that the Levites cannot dedicate it.

notes.dh: שאף רבי שמעון לא נחלק עליו כו'
notes.he: והכי משמע מילתיה דרבי נראין דברי ר' יהודה לר' שמעון בקרקעות שדברי ר"ש במטלטלין:
notes.en: For even Rabbi Shimon disagreed with him only etc.: and this is the meaning of Rabbi’s statement: the statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears correct to Rabbi Shimon with regard to land, for Rabbi Shimon’s statement concerns movable property.

notes.he: לא (לא) לעולם סבירא ליה לר' שמעון דמקרקעי אין מחרימין והכי קאמר רבי נראין דברי ר' יהודה לר' שמעון דלויים אין מחרימין בקרקעות דכתיב כי אחוזת עולם היא להם שאף רבי שמעון לא נחלק עליו כו']:
notes.en: No; actually Rabbi Shimon holds that land may not be dedicated, and this is what it means: Rabbi says, the statement of Rabbi Yehuda appears correct to Rabbi Shimon, that Levites may not dedicate land, as it is written, “For that is their perpetual possession,” for even Rabbi Shimon disagreed with him only etc.

messages.caption: May priests and Levites dedicate their property? Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Shimon as the Gemara explains him, and Rabbi.

messages.text: One who dedicated movable property may give it to any priest that he wishes, as it is stated: “Everything dedicated in Israel

notes.dh: החרים מטלטלין נותנן לכל כהן שירצה שנאמר כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה
notes.he: אין זה עיקר דרש דהא קרא איצטריך כדדריש ליה לקמיה נתנו לכהן הרי הוא כחולין לכל דבריו שנאמר כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה והא דאמר הכא נותנן לכל כהן שירצה מסברא הוא כמו תרומה שנותנה לכל כהן ואין צריך ליתנה לכהן שבאותו משמר ועוד אי הוי עיקר דרשא מאי הא דפריך לקמן ליקיש מטלטלין לקרקעות והלא גזירת הכתוב היא אלא ש"מ דלאו עיקר דרשה הוא זה:
notes.en: One who dedicated movable property gives it to any priest he wishes, as it is stated, “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours”: This is not the main derivation, since that verse is needed for what is expounded below (29a): Once he has given it to the priest it is like non-sacred property in every respect, as it is stated, “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours.” What is said here, that he gives them to any priest he wishes, is from reasoning, like teruma, which one gives to any priest and need not give to a priest of that watch. Furthermore, if it were the main derivation, what is the challenge below, “Let one juxtapose movable property to land”? It is a decree of the verse! Rather, learn from this that it is not the main derivation.

notes.he: בישראל קא מיירי:
notes.en: One who dedicated movable property: it is speaking of an Israelite.

messages.text: shall be yours” (Numbers 18:14), i.e., for Aaron and any of his descendants. But if one dedicated his fields, he gives them to a priest of that priestly watch which is currently serving in the Temple, as it is stated: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest” (Leviticus 27:21). And one derives a verbal analogy between “to the priest” here and “to the priest” from a verse (Numbers 5:8) discussing property robbed from a convert.

verse.he: וְהָיָה הַשָּׂדֶה בְּצֵאתוֹ בַיֹּבֵל קֹדֶשׁ לַיהֹוָה כִּשְׂדֵה הַחֵרֶם לַכֹּהֵן תִּהְיֶה אֲחֻזָּתוֹ׃
verse.en: when it is released in the jubilee, the land shall be holy to GOD, as land proscribed; it becomes the priest’s holding.

notes.he: לאהרן קאמר ליה רחמנא וכל זרעו בכלל:
notes.en: Shall be yours: the Merciful One said this to Aaron, and all his descendants are included.

notes.dh: שנאמר כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה
notes.he: לאיזה כהן שירצה יתנם כלומר שטובת הנאה שלו:
notes.en: As it is stated, “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours”: he gives them to whichever priest he wishes; that is, the benefit of choosing is his.

messages.text: The halakha in that case is that if one took an oath that he did not rob a convert, and then after the convert died and left no descendants he admitted to taking a false oath, he must give the stolen property to the priests of the priestly watch currently serving in the Temple.
And there, in the case of property robbed from a convert, from where do we derive that it is given to the priests of the current priestly watch? As it is taught in a baraita:

In the verse: “But if the man has no kinsman to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt that is made shall be the Lord’s, to the priest” (Numbers 5:8), the phrase: “Shall be the Lord’s, to the priest,” indicates that God has acquired the restitution for the guilt and has given it to the priest of that priestly watch.

verse.he: וְאִם־אֵין לָאִישׁ גֹּאֵל לְהָשִׁיב הָאָשָׁם אֵלָיו הָאָשָׁם הַמּוּשָׁב לַיהֹוָה לַכֹּהֵן מִלְּבַד אֵיל הַכִּפֻּרִים אֲשֶׁר יְכַפֶּר־בּוֹ עָלָיו׃
verse.en: If that party [is deceased and] has no kin to whom restitution can be made, the amount repaid shall go to GOD for the priest—in addition to the ram of expiation with which expiation is made on their behalf.

notes.he: בגזל הגר הכתוב מדבר שהרי בישראל אין לך אדם מישראל שאין לו גואלין אלא הגוזל את הגר ונשבע והודה ואחר כך מת משלם קרן וחומש לכהן ואשם למזבח ואמרינן בפרק הגוזל בב"ק (דף קי.) האשם זה הקרן המושב זה החומש מלבד איל הכיפורים זה איל אשם שמביא על שבועת שקר שנשבע:
notes.en: The restitution for guilt that is made shall be the Lord’s, to the priest: the verse speaks of robbery from a convert, for among Israelites there is no one without kinsmen. Rather, one who robbed a convert, swore, admitted, and afterward [the convert] died, pays the principal and the fifth to the priest and [brings] a guilt offering for the altar. And we say in chapter HaGozel in Bava Kamma (110a): “The restitution for guilt”: this is the principal; “that is made”: this is the fifth; “besides the ram of atonement”: this is the ram of the guilt offering that he brings for the false oath he swore.

notes.he: בגזל הגר מישתעי דדרשי' לקרא הכי אם [אין] לאיש גואל דהיינו גר דאין לו גואלים]:
notes.en: As it is taught, “To the Lord, to the priest”: the verse speaks of robbery from a convert, for we expound the verse thus: “If the man has no kinsman”: this is a convert, who has no kinsmen.

messages.text: Do you say the restitution is given to the priest of that priestly watch; or perhaps is it necessary only for it to be given to any priest to whom the robber wishes to give it?

When the same verse says: “Besides the ram of the atonement, whereby atonement shall be made for him,” this indicates that the verse speaks of a priest of that priestly watch, i.e., the watch that is currently involved in sacrificing offerings.

notes.he: דה"ק קרא שלכהן המכפר בו באיל הכפורים יהא קרן וחומש:
notes.en: Here the verse speaks of a priest of that watch: for this is what the verse means: to the priest who atones for him with the ram of atonement shall the principal and the fifth belong.

notes.he: אשר יכפר בו עליו הוי אומר בכהן שבאותו משמר שעובד ומקריב קרבנות הכתוב מדבר:
notes.en: “Whereby atonement shall be made for him”: you must say that the verse speaks of a priest of that watch, who serves and sacrifices the offerings.

messages.text: With regard to a field that was consecrated by its owner and was not redeemed by him, which goes out of his possession and passes to the possession of the priests at the Jubilee Year, one gives it to the members of the priestly watch serving when the Jubilee Year occurred, i.e., the watch serving at the beginning of the Jubilee Year.
messages.lead: § Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin states another halakha involving property that is given to the priests.

notes.he: רב חייא בר אבין קאמר לה:
notes.en: A field that goes out etc.: Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin says it.

notes.dh: שדה היוצאה לכהנים ביובל נותנין (למי) [למשמר] שפגע בו יובל
notes.he: האי מלתא אינו מן הברייתא אלא ממילתא דרבי חייא בר אבין אמר רב חסדא:
notes.en: A field that goes out to the priests at the Jubilee is given to the watch on which the Jubilee fell: this statement is not from the baraita, but from the statement of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin [that] Rav Ḥisda said.

notes.he: שחל יובל ליכנס בתוך משמרו:
notes.en: He gives it to the watch on which the Jubilee fell: that the Jubilee began during its watch.

messages.text: A dilemma was raised before the Sages: If the beginning of the Jubilee Year occurred on Shabbat, which is the day on which the priestly watches rotate, what is the halakha? Which priestly watch receives the property?

notes.he: יובל בשבת דמשמרות מתחלפות וחל בו יום הכיפורים בו ביום לאיזו יתן:
notes.en: It fell on: [that is,] the Jubilee [began] on Shabbat, when the watches change over, and Yom Kippur fell on it, on that very day: to which [watch] should he give it?

messages.text: One gives it to the watch that leaves the service of the Temple on that Shabbat.

notes.he: שברשותו התחיל היובל אמש:
notes.en: To the outgoing watch: for the Jubilee began in its domain the previous evening.

notes.he: פגע בו בשבת אם חל יובל ליכנס בשבת ובשבת עובדין ב' משמרות משמר היוצא ומשמר הנכנס לאיזה משמר הוא נותנה. נותנה למשמר היוצא הואיל והוא העובד שהקריב תמידין אמש והיום בשחרית:
notes.en: It fell on Shabbat: if the Jubilee began on Shabbat, and on Shabbat two watches serve, the outgoing watch and the incoming watch, to which watch does he give it? He gives it to the outgoing watch, since it is the one serving: it sacrificed the daily offerings last evening and this morning.

messages.text: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with these statements:

notes.he: דבתר התחלה אזלינן:
notes.en: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said: It is taught in accordance with this: that we go by the beginning.

messages.text: You are found to say that both the Jubilee Year, when fields that were sold are returned to their owners, and the Sabbatical Year, when debts are canceled, abrogate at once, i.e., at the same time, except that the Jubilee Year abrogates at its beginning and the Sabbatical Year abrogates at its end.

notes.he: הואיל ושנת מ"ט התחיל שביעית ושנה של אחריה יובל:
notes.en: You are found to say: since the forty-ninth year is the Sabbatical Year, and the year after it is the Jubilee.

notes.dh: אחד יובל ואחד שביעית משמטין כאחד
notes.he: ביום אחד שביעית משמטת הלואת כספים ויובל מכירת קרקעות אלא שהיובל כו':
notes.en: Both the Jubilee and the Sabbatical Year release at once: on one day, the Sabbatical Year releasing money loans and the Jubilee releasing sales of land, except that the Jubilee etc.

notes.he: כלומר ששמיטתן פוגעין זה בזה לפי ששנת מ"ט היא שביעית ושנת נ' היא יובל אלא שהיובל משמט בתחילה ובשביעית בסופה:
notes.en: Both the Jubilee and the Sabbatical Year release at once: that is, their releases meet one another, since the forty-ninth year is the Sabbatical Year and the fiftieth year is the Jubilee; except that the Jubilee releases at its beginning and the Sabbatical Year at its end.

messages.text: In other words, the evening of Rosh HaShana at the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year, which is the forty-ninth year of the Jubilee cycle, is also the beginning of the Jubilee Year, which is the fiftieth year. At this time, all debts and land purchases are abrogated, and consecrated fields that were not redeemed become the property of the priests. Accordingly, if Rosh HaShana occurs on a Shabbat, the priestly watch that ends their service receives the fields, as the priestly watches rotate only in the morning.

Why does the baraita state: Except that? This statement indicates that the Sabbatical Year and the Jubilee Year abrogate simultaneously despite the fact that the Jubilee Year abrogates at its beginning. On the contrary, this halakha is due to that very reason, i.e., they abrogate simultaneously because the Jubilee Year abrogates at its beginning and the Sabbatical Year at its end.
messages.quote: except that the Jubilee Year abrogates at its beginning

notes.he: טעמא דשניהם משמטים ביום אחד מש"ה דשביעית בסופה ויובל בתחילתו דהשתא אשתכח דבין [השמשות] של ערב שבת יובל נפקא שביעית וההיא שעתא תרוייהו משמטין:
notes.en: On the contrary: the reason that both release on one day is precisely that the Sabbatical Year [releases] at its end and the Jubilee at its beginning; for then it turns out that at twilight on the eve of the Jubilee the Sabbatical Year departs, and at that moment both release.

notes.he: כלומר טעמא מאי משמטין כאחד מפני שהשביעית משמטת בסופה לכספים ויובל בתחילתה אלא תריץ הכי במקום אלא תני מפני שהיובל בתחילה כו']:
notes.en: On the contrary, it is because of this: that is, what is the reason they release at once? Because the Sabbatical Year releases money at its end and the Jubilee at its beginning. So instead of “except that,” correct it and teach: “because the Jubilee at its beginning etc.”

messages.text: In fact one should say the baraita as follows: They abrogate at the same time, due to the fact that the Jubilee Year abrogates at its beginning and the Sabbatical Year at its end.

notes.he: תני הכי משמטין כאחד מפני שהיובל בתחילתו ושביעית בסופה:
notes.en: Rather: teach it this way: they release at once because the Jubilee [releases] at its beginning and the Sabbatical Year at its end. [Rashi’s text of the Gemara reads “rather, teach” where ours reads “say.”]

messages.text: Granted, it is clear that the Sabbatical Year abrogates at its end, as it is written: “At the end of every seven years you shall make a release” (Deuteronomy 15:1).

verse.en: Every seventh year you shall practice remission of debts.

notes.he: בהשמטת כספים מיירי דאי בהשמטת קרקע לענין זריעה וחרישה מתחילת שביעית משמטין:
notes.en: Granted, the Sabbatical Year releases at its end: this speaks of the release of money; for with regard to the release of land, as to sowing and plowing, they release from the beginning of the Sabbatical Year.

notes.he: דכתיב מקץ שבע שנים בסופה תעשה שמטה וזה דבר השמטה וגו':
notes.en: As it is written: “At the end of every seven years you shall make a release,” and “This is the manner of the release…” [Deuteronomy 15:2].

messages.text: But does the Jubilee Year abrogate at its very beginning? It abrogates only ten days later, on Yom Kippur, as it is written: “On Yom Kippur shall you make proclamation with the shofar throughout all your land…and you shall return every man to his possession” (Leviticus 25:9–10).

verse.he: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ שׁוֹפַר תְּרוּעָה בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִעִי בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ בְּיוֹם הַכִּפֻּרִים תַּעֲבִירוּ שׁוֹפָר בְּכׇל־אַרְצְכֶם׃
verse.en: Then you shall sound the horn loud; in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month—the Day of Atonement—you shall have the horn sounded throughout your land

notes.he: ביום הכפורים חייל יובל והיאך משמטין כאחד והרי עשרה ימים הן בין סוף שביעית להתחלת יובל:
notes.en: But the Jubilee at its beginning? The Jubilee takes effect on Yom Kippur. How, then, do they release at once? There are ten days between the end of the Sabbatical Year and the beginning of the Jubilee.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this baraita? It is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, who says:

notes.he: דמשמטין כאחד:
notes.en: Whose is this: [the teaching] that they release at once?

notes.he: ר' ישמעאל בנו של ר' יוחנן בן ברוקא היא]:
notes.en: It is Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka.

messages.text: It is from Rosh HaShana that the Jubilee Year takes effect.

notes.he: דרבי ישמעאל בפרק קמא דר"ה (דף ח:):
notes.en: [The view of] Rabbi Yishmael is in the first chapter of Rosh HaShana (8b).

messages.text: The Gemara returns to the statement of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin that one who dedicates his movable property may give it to a priest of his choosing, whereas one who dedicates his land gives it to members of the current priestly watch. Ḥizkiyya bar Biluto heard this statement and went and said the following difficulty before Rabbi Abbahu:
messages.quote: One who dedicated movable property may give it to any priest that he wishes

notes.he: להא דרב חייא בר אבין:
notes.en: Ḥizkiyya bar Biluto heard it: this statement of Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin.

notes.he: להא דאמר חייא בר אבין:
notes.en: Ḥizkiyya bar Biluto heard it: this that Ḥiyya bar Avin said.

messages.text: @Rabbi Abbahu But let one juxtapose movable property to land, as the verse states: “That a man may dedicate to the Lord of all that he has, whether of man or animal, or of his ancestral field” (Leviticus 27:28). If so, movable property must also be given to members of the current priestly watch.

notes.he: דחרם:
notes.en: And let one juxtapose movable property: of ḥerem.

notes.he: דחרם דהא איתקיש דכתיב מכל אשר לו ומשדה אחוזתו ולימא דליתבו נמי מטלטלין לכהן שבאותו משמר:
notes.en: To land: of ḥerem, since they are juxtaposed, as it is written, “of all that he has … or of his ancestral field”; so let us say that movable property too is given to a priest of that watch.

notes.he: אמר ליה אמאי אמר נותנן לכל כהן שירצה וליקוש מטלטלין לקרקעות [דליתנן לכהן שבאותו משמר]:
notes.en: He said it before Rabbi Abbahu: he said to him: Why did he say one gives them to any priest he wishes? Let one juxtapose movable property to land, so that one gives them to a priest of that watch.

messages.text: Is it not a dispute between tanna’im? As there are those who juxtapose and there are those who do not juxtapose, in accordance with the earlier explanation of the Gemara that this is the basis for the dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon with regard to whether or not Levites may dedicate movable property.
messages.quote: But let one juxtapose movable property to land

notes.he: ר' יהודה ור"ש איפלגי לעיל בהא דרבי יהודה מקיש ור"ש לא מקיש:
notes.en: Is it not a dispute of tanna’im: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon disagreed about this above: Rabbi Yehuda juxtaposes and Rabbi Shimon does not juxtapose.

notes.he: היא דרבי יהודה מקיש מטלטלי לקרקעות ור' שמעון לא מקיש ור' חייא סבר לה כמאן דלא מקיש:
notes.en: Is it not a dispute of tanna’im: Rabbi Yehuda juxtaposes movable property to land and Rabbi Shimon does not juxtapose, and Rabbi Ḥiyya holds like the one who does not juxtapose.

messages.text: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin holds in accordance with the opinion of the one who says we do not juxtapose movable property and land.

notes.he: וא"ת הא דאמרן לעיל בשלמא כהנים אין מחרימין דחרמים שלהם והלא שדה חרמים צריך ליתנם לכהן שבאותו משמר וא"כ אם החרים כהן שדהו אם אינו במשמרתו אמאי אינו צריך ליתנה לכהן שבאותו משמר וצ"ל דלרווחא דמילתא אמר הכי שהרי אם החרים כהן שדהו אינו חרם דכתיב אחוזת עולם הוא להם ואע"ג דגבי לוים הוא דכתיב מסתמא לכהנים נמי הכי הוא ואם החרים הכהן מטלטלים למאן דמקיש פשיטא דאינו יכול להחרים ואפילו למאן דלא מקיש החרמים שלהן כדאמרן נותנו לכל כהן שירצה וניחא נמי הא דאמר לעיל ורבי שמעון בשלמא כהנים כדאמרי' ומשום מטלטלין הוא דאמר הכי אע"ג דאין מקיש מ"מ החרמים שלהם אבל בקרקעות אחוזת עולם דכתיב גבי לוים ה"ה לכהנים כן:
notes.en: In accordance with the one who does not juxtapose: You might ask about what we said above, “Granted, priests may not dedicate, as the dedications are theirs”: but dedicated fields must be given to a priest of that watch! If so, if a priest dedicated his field when it is not his watch, why need he not give it to a priest of that watch? One must say that this was said only to strengthen the point. For if a priest dedicated his field, it is no ḥerem, as it is written, “For that is their perpetual possession”; and although that is written about Levites, presumably the same holds for priests. And if a priest dedicated movable property, according to the one who juxtaposes it is obvious that he cannot dedicate it; and even according to the one who does not juxtapose, the dedications are theirs, as we said, since one gives them to any priest he wishes. This also settles what was said above, “And Rabbi Shimon: granted, priests, as we said”: he said it because of movable property, since although he does not juxtapose, the dedications are theirs in any case; but as for land, “perpetual possession,” written about Levites, applies equally to priests.

messages.caption: To which priest does the dedicated property go? Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin’s rulings and the dilemma of a Jubilee that begins on Shabbat.

messages.text: Mishna

Dedications of property for priests, unlike consecrations of property for Temple maintenance, have no redemption; rather, one gives it to the priests, and it is their property in every sense, like teruma.

notes.he: חרמים שהחרימם כדי לתתם לכהן אין להם פדיון דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ח) לא ימכר ולא יגאל אבל חרמי בדק הבית יש להם פדיון דאדעתא דהכי אחרמינהו דהא אין ראוי לבדק הבית אלא מעות:
notes.en: Mishna. Dedications for priests: dedications that one dedicated in order to give them to the priest have no redemption, as it is written, “It shall not be sold or redeemed” (Leviticus 27:28). But dedications for Temple maintenance have redemption, for he dedicated them with this in mind, since only money is suitable for Temple maintenance.

notes.he: פי' חרמים (ליתן) הניתנים לכהנים אין להן פדיון כדכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ח) לא ימכר ולא יגאל וע"כ בחרמי כהנים איירי אע"ג דסתמא כתיב דאי בחרמי בדק הבית פשיטא דנפדין הן כדי לעשות מהן צרכי בדק הבית:
notes.en: Dedications for priests: that is, dedications given to the priests have no redemption, as it is written, “It shall not be sold or redeemed” (Leviticus 27:28). And [that verse] must be speaking of dedications for priests, even though it is written without specification, for if it were about dedications for Temple maintenance, it is obvious that they are redeemed, in order to use [the money] for the needs of Temple maintenance.

notes.he: חרמי כהנים שישראל מחרים לדעת שיבוא ליד כהן אין להן פדיון אלא ליתנם לכהן כדכתיב כל חרם בישראל לך יהיה:
notes.en: Dedications for priests, which an Israelite dedicates intending that they reach a priest’s hand, have no redemption; rather, he gives them to the priests, as it is written, “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours.”

messages.text: Dedications dedicated without specification of their purpose are designated for Temple maintenance, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord” (Leviticus 27:28).

notes.he: סתם חרמים שלא הזכיר כהן:
notes.en: Unspecified dedications: where he did not mention a priest.

messages.text: Dedications dedicated without specification of their purpose are designated for priests, as it is stated with regard to one who consecrated a field and did not redeem it: “As a field dedicated; its possession shall be to the priest” (Leviticus 27:21), indicating that a non-specific dedication belongs to the priest.

If so, why is it stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord”? This comes to teach that dedication takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity. If one consecrated an animal for sacrifice and then dedicated it, the dedication takes effect. Nevertheless, it does not take effect on the body of the animal; rather, it applies to the owner’s financial stake in the offering.

notes.dh: שחל החרם על קדשי קדשים כו'
notes.he: כדמפרש מחרים אדם את קדשיו וכו' והיאך מוחרמים והלא אינו שלו אלא אם נדר הן דאמר הרי עלי עולה והפריש בהמה לנדרו ואחר כך החרימה הואיל והוא חייב באחריותה אם מתה או נגנבה נמצאת שלו היא והוא נותן כל דמיה לכהן ואת הבהמה יקריב לנדרו דהא ודאי אית ליה פדיון דלאו גופה איחרם דלאו דידיה הוא:
notes.en: That it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order etc.: as it explains: A person may dedicate his consecrated animals etc. And how are they dedicated? They are not his! Rather, if they are a vow, where he said, “It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a burnt offering,” and set aside an animal for his vow and afterward dedicated it: since he bears responsibility for it if it dies or is stolen, it turns out to be his, and he gives its full value to the priest and sacrifices the animal for his vow. For it certainly has redemption, since the animal itself was not dedicated, as it is not his.

notes.dh: שחל החרם על קדשי קדשים ועל קדשים קלים
notes.he: כיצד כדמפרש לקמן לא שיהא יכול להתפיס הן עצמן לשום חרם או לשום דבר אחר דאין הקדש חל על הקדשים אלא כדמפרש מחרים אדם את קדשיו בין קדשי קדשים ובין קדשים קלים אם נדר הם שאמר עלי שחייב באחריותו נותן דמיהם לכהנים מפני שהחרימן והן עצמן אינן לשום חרם אלא קרבין לשום חובתו ואם הן נדבה שאינו חייב באחריותן לא חשיבי ממונו ואין נותן לכהנים בשביל החרם אלא טובתה מה שהוא רשאי ליטול הימנה טובת הנאה ומפרש כיצד נותן את טובתה אמר שור זה עולה דלא אמר עלי דאינו חייב באחריותו ואח"כ אמר הרי הוא חרם אומדין כמה אדם כו'. אע"ג דנדבה הוא ואין חייב באחריותן אכתי אדם שאינו מחוייב עולה אי משכח לה בזול יקנה אותה ואותה אחריות הוי עליו ונותן אותן דמים. פירוש אחר אומדין כמה אדם כהן שאינו ממשמר זה שעובד רוצה ליתן להמתנדב משור זה שימתין לו שיתנו לו (להקריבו) להעלהו עולה בזמן משמרתו כדי שיזכה בעורו כמו שאותו כהן היה נותן לו כך וכך יתן זה שהחרימו לכהנים וזהו קדשי קדשים:
notes.en: That it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity: how? As it explains below. Not that he can attach the offerings themselves to some ḥerem or anything else, for consecration does not take effect on consecrated items; rather, as it explains: A person may dedicate his consecrated animals, whether offerings of the most sacred order or offerings of lesser sanctity. If they are a vow, where he said “incumbent upon me,” so that he is responsible for it, he gives their value to the priests because he dedicated them, and the animals themselves are not [treated] as ḥerem but are sacrificed for his obligation. And if they are a gift offering, for which he is not responsible, they do not count as his property, and he gives the priests on account of the ḥerem only its benefit, the monetary benefit he is permitted to take from it. And it explains how he gives its benefit: he said, “This bull is a burnt offering,” not saying “incumbent upon me,” so that he is not responsible for it, and afterward he said, “It is ḥerem”: one estimates how much a person etc. Even though it is a gift offering and he is not responsible for it, still, a person who is not obligated to bring a burnt offering would buy one if he found it cheaply, and that responsibility would be upon him; and he gives that sum. Another explanation: one estimates how much a person, a priest who is not of the watch now serving, would want to give the donor for this bull so that he would wait for him and give it to him to sacrifice as a burnt offering during his own watch, so that he would acquire its hide. As much as that priest would give him, so much this one who dedicated it gives the priests. And this is [the case of] offerings of the most sacred order.

messages.text: A person may dedicate his sacrificial animals, both offerings of the most sacred order and offerings of lesser sanctity. If the offering he dedicated was the object of a vow, e.g., if he said: It is incumbent upon me to sacrifice a burnt offering, since he is obligated to replace such offerings they are considered his property, and therefore he gives their value to the priests.

And if the offering he dedicated was a gift offering, e.g., if he said: This animal is a burnt offering, in which case he is not obligated to replace the animal, he gives the monetary benefit that he has in them.

notes.he: היא דאינו חייב באחריותה אם היתה מתה הא ודאי לא חייל חרם דלאו דידיה:
notes.en: And if it is a gift offering: where he is not responsible for it if it dies, certainly the ḥerem does not take effect [on the animal’s value], since it is not his.

messages.text: For example, if he said: This bull is a burnt offering, one estimates how much money a person would be willing to give in order to sacrifice the animal as a voluntary burnt offering, even though he is not permitted to do so.

notes.he: טובת הנאה שיש לו בה יתן לכהן כיצד שור זה עולה והחרימו אומדין כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בשור זה להקריבו עולה שאינו חייב כלומר אדם שאינו חייב עולה אם ימצא בזול נוטלו להקריב דורון לקונו וכאותן דמים יתן זה שזו היא טובת הנאה שיש לו בה שהרי אם מתה או נגנבה אינו חייב באחריותה ומשהפרישה יצא ידי חובתו ומעתה אם תאבד אינו מפסיד אלא שלא הקריב דורון לקונו הרי שהפסיד העלאת עולה שאינו חייב. ואית ספרים דכתב בהן להעלות עולה שאינו רשאי והיא היא:
notes.en: Rather, by its benefit: the monetary benefit he has in it he gives to the priest. How? [He said,] “This bull is a burnt offering,” and dedicated it: one estimates how much a person would want to give for this bull to sacrifice it as a burnt offering that he is not obligated [to bring]. That is to say, a person who is not obligated to bring a burnt offering, if he finds one cheaply, takes it to sacrifice as a gift to his Maker; and this man gives that sum. For this is the monetary benefit he has in it: if it died or was stolen he is not responsible for it, since once he set it aside he fulfilled his obligation, and from then on, if it is lost, he loses only that he has not sacrificed a gift to his Maker. So what he has lost is the offering of a burnt offering that he is not obligated [to bring]. Some books read, “to sacrifice a burnt offering that he is not permitted,” and it is the same thing.

notes.he: לשון חייב נושה (שמות כב) מתרגמינן רשיא:
notes.en: Permitted [rashai]: a term meaning obligated, [as] “a creditor” [noshe] (Exodus 22:24) is rendered in the Targum rashya.

notes.dh: אומדין כמה אדם רוצה ליתן בשור זה להעלותו עולה אע"פ שאינו רשאי
notes.he: (ליתן) פירוש שאינו חייב כמו נושה דמתרגמינן רשיא כך פירש"י ולפ"ז אומר הרב רבי יעקב בר שמשון הא דאיתא בפ"ק דקדושין (דף לג. ושם) אין בעלי אומניות רשאין לעמוד בפני תלמידי חכמים בשעה שעוסקים במלאכתן מיירי אפילו בעסוקין במלאכתם ורשאין ר"ל חייבין כמו אע"פ שאינו רשאי דהכא ר"ל אע"פ שאינו חייב ואי מיירי במלאכת אחרים ניחא למימר רשאין ממש:
notes.en: One estimates how much a person would want to give for this bull to sacrifice it as a burnt offering, even though he is not rashai: that is, he is not obligated, as noshe [a creditor] is rendered in the Targum rashya; so Rashi explained. Accordingly, the master Rabbi Ya’akov bar Shimshon says that what is taught in the first chapter of Kiddushin (33a), “Craftsmen are not rashain to stand before Torah scholars while they are engaged in their work,” applies even when they are engaged in their own work, and rashain means “obligated,” like “even though he is not rashai” here, which means “even though he is not obligated.” And if it speaks of work for others, one may well read rashain in its plain sense [“permitted”].

notes.he: (בתמורה בישראל בקדשים) [שאינו רשאי] כלומר כיון שאינו חייב באחריותו אינו נותן דמי כלו אלא טובת הנאתו כדאמרן:
notes.en: [The printed text here is corrupt; an editor’s note proposes the reading:] Even though he is not rashai: that is, he is not obligated at all to sacrifice a burnt offering; that is, since he is not responsible for it, he does not give its full value, only its monetary benefit, as we said.

messages.text: With regard to a firstborn animal, whether it is unblemished or whether it is blemished, its owner may dedicate it.

notes.he: הבכור כשהוא ברשות ישראל בין תם בין בעל מום מחרימין אותו טובת הנאתו ולא דמי כולו שאינו חייב באחריותו וכיצד פודין אותו כלומר כיצד שמין טובת הנאתו אומדים כמה אדם מישראל רוצה ליתן בבכור זה לבעלים שיתננו לבן בתו כהן או לבן אחותו כהן כך יתן זה שהחרימו לכהנים:
notes.en: And offerings of lesser sanctity, how? A firstborn, while it is in an Israelite’s possession, whether unblemished or blemished, may be dedicated, [and he gives] its monetary benefit and not its full value, since he is not responsible for it. And how does one redeem it? That is, how does one assess its benefit? One estimates how much an Israelite would want to give the owner for this firstborn so that he would give it to his daughter’s son who is a priest, or to his sister’s son who is a priest; so much this one who dedicated it gives the priests.

messages.text: And how does one assess the payment required to redeem it? One estimates how much an Israelite person would be willing to give in exchange for that firstborn in order to give it to a priest who is his daughter’s son or to a priest who is his sister’s son.

notes.he: דהבכור גופו אינו מוחרם שהרי אינו שלו אלא לכהן:
notes.en: And how does one redeem it: for the firstborn itself is not dedicated, since it is not his but the priest’s.

notes.he: מישראל רוצה ליתן לבעל הבית זה ליתן בכורו לבן בתו כהן או לבן אחותו ואותה טובת הנאה יתן בעל הבית זה לכהן בשביל החרם. ודוקא נקט בן בתו ובן אחותו כהן דההיא דיהיב לה להך טובת הנאה ליהוי ישראל אבל בן בנו כהן ובן אחיו כהן דהאי דיהיב לה להך טובת הנאה הוי כהן לא מצי יהיב ליה אגרא ואע"ג דלאו משום דידיה יהיב ליה כיון דלדידיה נמי חזי הבכור נראה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות לדוש ולזרות כדי שיתנו לו תרומותיו בשכרו ואשתכח דלא שקיל בתורת תרומה אלא בתורת שכר והכי אמרינן בבכורות בפ' עד כמה (בכורות דף כו:):
notes.en: Rather, one estimates how much a person, an Israelite, would want to give this householder so that he gives his firstborn to his daughter’s son who is a priest, or to his sister’s son; and that monetary benefit this householder gives to the priest on account of the ḥerem. It says specifically a daughter’s son and a sister’s son who are priests, because then the one who gives him that benefit is an Israelite. But with a son’s son who is a priest, or a brother’s son who is a priest, the one who would give him that benefit is a priest, and he may not pay a fee for it: even though he is not giving for his own sake, since the firstborn is fit for him too, he looks like a priest who helps at the threshing floors, threshing and winnowing, so that they will give him their teruma as his wage, and it turns out that he takes it not as teruma but as a wage. And so we say in Bekhorot, in chapter Ad Kamma (Bekhorot 26b).

notes.dh: לבן בתו או לבן אחותו כהן
notes.he: ולא מצי' למימר לבן בנו או לבן אחיו דכיון דחזיא ליה הוי ליה ככהן המסייע בבית הגרנות כדאיתא בפ' עד כמה (בכורות כו:) וכן פירש"י:
notes.en: To his daughter’s son or his sister’s son who is a priest: one cannot say his son’s son or his brother’s son, because since [the firstborn] is fit for him, he is like a priest who helps at the threshing floors, as is found in chapter Ad Kamma (Bekhorot 26b). And so Rashi explained.

messages.text: The Gemara on this mishna begins on 29a.
